literal: Measure knew-they heart-in virtue like will-stand theft knew-they heart-in deceit.
translation: Just as virtue abides in the hearts of those who know their limits, deceit abides in the hearts of those who know theft.
modern: தங்கள் அளவை அறிந்து வாழ்பவர்களின் நெஞ்சில் அறம் நிலைத்து நிற்பது போல, திருடுவதை அறிந்தவர்களின் நெஞ்சில் வஞ்சனை நிலைத்து நிற்கும்.
explanation: The couplet contrasts two types of people and what resides in their hearts. For those who know their proper measure and limits, virtue stands firmly in their minds. In the same way, for those who are familiar with theft, deceit and concealment constantly occupy their thoughts. The word 'கரவு' means deceit or hiding, showing that a thief's mind is always troubled by the need to conceal their actions.
